title: Learn Product Management
tagline: From problem briefs to shipped outcomes — decide what to build and why
description: A three-level curriculum for Product Managers. Learn to frame problems, write requirements teams can build from, run discovery with design and engineering, and own outcomes with roadmaps, metrics, and experiments — not a backlog of features.
prerequisites: Comfort writing clearly for other people (emails, briefs, or docs)
Willingness to talk to users and sit with incomplete information
Basic numeracy: percentages, trends, and reading a simple chart

levels.title: Product Foundations
levels.goal: Frame a problem, write requirements a team can build from, and prioritize a first backlog

topics.title: The PM role
items: Discovery vs. delivery — and why both are the job
PM vs. project manager vs. founder vs. designer
What you own: problem, outcome, and communication — not the code

topics.title: How product teams work
items: The trio: product, design, and engineering
Stakeholders: sales, support, ops, and leadership
A feature's path from idea to release

topics.title: Problem statements
items: Who hurts, how often, and what they do today
Problem vs. solution: keep the brief solution-agnostic
Opportunity size without fake TAM slides

topics.title: Lightweight discovery
items: Five customer conversations beat a survey of 200 strangers
Jobs to be done and the job-to-be-done interview
Shadowing support tickets and sales calls

topics.title: Competitive & market awareness
items: Teardown: flows, pricing, and what they optimize for
Substitutes (including spreadsheets and WhatsApp groups)
When to ignore competitors and when not to

topics.title: User stories & acceptance criteria
items: As a / I want / so that — and when that template fails
Acceptance criteria that QA and engineering can test
Edge cases: empty, error, permission, and offline

topics.title: Specs teams can use
items: One-pager vs. PRD vs. ticket — pick the lightest that works
Scope: in, out, and later
Open questions and who will answer them

topics.title: Prioritization
items: Impact vs. effort, RICE, and MoSCoW
Must-haves vs. nice-to-haves for a first release
Saying no with a reason, not a delay

projects: Problem brief for a familiar product (mobile money, SACCO member app, or campus marketplace)
User stories and acceptance criteria for a small feature (e.g. bill-split or deposit confirmation)
Prioritized backlog of 10 items with a one-line rationale each
Competitive teardown of two similar products: flows, pricing, and what you would steal

levels.title: Shipping With Teams
levels.goal: Run discovery-to-delivery with design and engineering, and communicate a roadmap with trade-offs

topics.title: Ceremonies that earn their time
items: Sprint planning, standup, review, and retro — what each is for
Story points, capacity, and when estimates are theater
Definition of ready and definition of done

topics.title: Unblocking the team
items: Cutting scope mid-sprint without wrecking trust
Dependencies, blockers, and who owns the chase
Bugs vs. features: a simple triage rule

topics.title: Working with design
items: Briefing a designer: problem, constraints, and success
Commenting in Figma without designing in the margins
Usability findings that change the spec

topics.title: Working with engineering
items: Technical constraints as product input, not a veto
API contracts, feature flags, and rollout plans
Estimates, spikes, and when to spike vs. build

topics.title: Release communication
items: Release notes for users vs. internal changelog
Go / no-go: quality, support readiness, and known issues
Rollback and what you tell customers if it fails

topics.title: Product analytics basics
items: Activation, retention, and a North Star that is not vanity
Event naming and funnels you can actually trust
Reading a dashboard without overfitting last week's dip

topics.title: Experiments without overclaiming
items: Hypothesis, metric, and guardrail before you ship a test
Sample size and why a 3-day test is usually noise
When a qualitative study beats an A/B test

topics.title: Roadmaps that survive contact
items: Now / next / later vs. dated Gantt fiction
Themes and outcomes, not a list of tickets
Communicating trade-offs to leadership

topics.title: Stakeholder management
items: Sales and support as discovery channels
Escalations: what is a bug, a request, and a strategy debate
Written updates that replace status meetings

projects: Full PRD for a new feature (problem, users, scope, AC, analytics, risks)
Two-week sprint plan plus retro notes for a mock team
Now/next/later roadmap slide with three explicit trade-offs for leadership
Spec a KYC, checkout, or M-Pesa collection flow including empty, error, and retry states

levels.title: Strategy, Outcomes & Influence
levels.goal: Own outcomes, not output — strategy, experiments, and decisions that survive scrutiny

topics.title: Strategy that is not a slogan

Connecting company goals to a product area
Kill criteria: when a bet is over

Sequencing: what must be true before the next bet

topics.title: Loops and funnels

Pricing, packaging, and willingness to pay at a working level

topics.title: Experiment systems
items: Experiment briefs, holdouts, and peeking
Feature flags as product, not only as engineering
Post-ship reviews: what we learned, not just what we launched

topics.title: Decision-grade communication
items: Options, recommendation, and what you would need to change your mind
Executive vs. operator audiences
Writing that survives a 15-minute read

topics.title: Ethics & constraints
items: Dark patterns, consent, and data you should not collect
Accessibility and inclusion as product requirements
Regulatory and payments constraints (KYC, AML, consumer protection) as design input

projects: Strategy memo plus a two-quarter roadmap with kill criteria
Experiment design for an activation or retention bet (hypothesis, metric, sample, guardrails)
KPI tree and dashboard brief for a product area (e.g. collections, active members, or onboarding)
Stakeholder readout with a recommendation, alternatives, and limitations
